children: Shares in Crest Nicholson fell after the U.K. home builder warned it would post an operating loss in its fiscal year and trimmed its sales expectations.
In morning trading, London-listed shares were down 13% at 53.10 pence, and are down 62% in the year to date.

The company said Thursday that it expects to post a loss before interest and taxes of around 10 million pounds ($13.5 million) for the year through  October compared with previous guidance of an operating profit of 5 million to 10 million pounds.

Crest Nicholson also lowered its full-year sales guidance to a range of 1,350 to 1,400 units from 1,400 to 1,500, citing more subdued market conditions than expected over the summer. The builder said open-market sales continue to lag as stretched buyer budgets and tight price competition take their toll.
Its net open-market sales rate per outlet per week--a key metric for the sector--for the past six weeks fell to 0.35 from 0.48 in the first half. For the same period last year, it was 0.55.

"Although the timing of a broader market recovery remains uncertain, the group is taking the right actions to protect liquidity and improve operational execution, while positioning the business for recovery when market conditions normalize," Chief Executive Martyn Clark said.

title: Crest Nicholson Shares Fall on Profit Warning
